Concentrated Solar Power

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
South Africa has 33 Renewable Energy power plants commissioned and by the end of next year there will be enough plants online to generate the same amount of power as Koeberg. By 2030 they will generate 17 800 MW of power. Globally there is a move towards renewable energy, the G7 announced this week that they intend to stop using all fossil fuels by the end of the century. South Africa is in a very unique position in that most of the country has sufficient sunshine all year to be totally solar powered. We can solve our electricity needs with Renewables which raises the question why we are pursuing Nuclear power at the cost of 1 Trillion Rand and that's without the costs of disposaling of the nuclear rods. Fracking for natural gas also makes no economic sense when the world price of oil is dropping.Since 2010 we have been embracing Renewables, this week Minister of Energy Tina Joemat-Petterssen commissioned 13 new renewable projects. Concentrated Solar Power or CSP has changed the whole solar power industry because its made solar energy storable and stable.

Further information:
Concentrated Solar Power or CSP is the new kid on the block when it comes to renewable energy. It focuses the solar energy and is able to store it for several hours after sunset and because of how it is stored it is more stable and accessible that coal fired power stations. A CSP plant can be switched onto the grid within 15 minutes whereas a coal plant takes hours to fire up. There are 7 CSP projects being built in South Africa, KaXu Solar 1 came online in March this year and producers 100 MWs and has 5 hours of power generation after dark. Bokspoort is nearing completion and will have 9 hours of storage generating 50MW power. Bokspoort has the largest storage capacity in the world.

Currently Eskom is burning the reserve generators to keep the lights on but these are fired by diesel and gas and costing a whopping R5 KW hour.CSP wind and Solar Voltaic electricity can supply that additional power at one fifth of the cost. Wind power costs 68c a KW hour and Solar Voltaic 85c a KW hour.

Globally 90% of the coal reserves will be economically exhausted by 2048 meaning that it will be so expensive to extract it won’t be economically viable. In South Africa we are on a plateau of Coal production but from here on it will start declining. Medupi will run out of coal half way through it life span. Currently it is estimated electricity generated by coal costs R1.05 but this cost will continue to rise. Photovoltic and wind energy is already cheaper that Coal, and CSP solar power will get cheaper as technology advances.

Swedish Company Ripasso which has used technology originally designed for the military and developed it for solar power generation which outstrips the performance of current solar voltaic panels. It consists of 100 sq meter solar dishes which rotate following the path of the sun, capturing 35% of solar energy which is then drives a Stirling engine. Stirling engines have no carbon emissions. The project has been piloted for the last 4 years in the Kalahari. The amount of power generated is 35% , 10 % higher than Solarvoltaic panels which capture only 23% and convert to the grid on 15%. Each dish can generate 75-85 megawatts of power which is enough for 24 average households for 1 year. If the same amount of power was generated by coal power station it would emit 81 metric tonnes of CO2 Carbon Emissions. They have a hybridized system that switches over to fuel to keep running at night. This system gives you power for 24 hours. Any kind of fuel can be used, from biofuel to gas.

KaXu Solar One plant it is a 100MW concentrated solar power (CSP) on a 1,100ha site. It's the first CSP plant in South Africa to using parabolic trough technology. It supplies clean energy to approximately 90,000 African homes while offsetting 315,000t of CO2 emissions per year. Khi Solar 1 also in partership with Spanish Company Abengoa uses tower technology and is about to come online.

The 4th project is purely South African and based at Stellenbosch University called Helio100. It is using entirely SA labour and materials and developing CSP Tower technology with much smaller dishes close to the ground which can project from 1km from any solar tower. It is part of the Solar Thermal Energy Research Group, the largest research unit of its kind worldwide.

Viewing Notes:
21/07/2015 04:22:46 PM

AC, GM
• Story will need a re-cut and another viewing please feels a little dull and it’s incredibly complex – hard to remember all the facts. Its very interesting but far too technical for viewers at the moment feels very, very complex.
• We don’t need it for Sunday at this point
• Your ten second teasers are lovely and so are your promos
• The tower and dishes are interesting, the fact we are poised to be world first, the links are very nice, visuals very nice, Prof from Stellen very good, nice to have the community.
• Start with the tower which is very interesting... need a narrative from there... you go home and don’t know whether you will have power – that context first, the fact we have biggest in Southern Hemisphere, (currently thereafter there is a LOT of info and its visually beautiful but it’s hard to follow the script).
• Spread the Stellenbosch prof throughout the story
• We didn’t get how much energy the big farm is giving to the grid
• And we don’t understand how many of those large round dishes you need to power the town nearby and even if they are plugged into the grid at all
• Please limit the shots of the informal settlement from the car – better to show the people, and the 2 fridges in the shack could be a way in to the story people in remote places with basic facilities will have a better quality of life...
• We didn’t use the sun enough – graphics of sun/universe showing how it moves
• Where else in the country would this work
• And what happens if there is cloud cover
• You say CSP too often, please explain concentrated solar power more often.
• There is a whole presentation by Elon Musk on YOUTUBE – use these visuals rather than your stills. We know you had a technical problem here.

Press Release:


Concentrated Solar Power
With even more solar radiation levels than the Sahara, South Africa has become the epicentre of a solar explosion. Renewable energy is big business and independent power producers the world over are scrambling to the Northern Cape for a spot in the sun. In a race to get off the grid, solar power stations are sprouting up from Upington to De Aar. With SA set to become a world player in the solar market, Carte Blanche asks whether load shedding could actually be a blessing in disguise?


Script:


Script: Nothings predictable in South Africa at the moment, except the sun is guaranteed to shine in the Northern Cape. With the second best solar radiation levels globally, even more than the Sahara, Independent power producers from around the world are scrambling to get their spot in the sun.
Link “It’s the new gold rush, energy from the skies to power industry and our everyday lives. The solar explosion is happening right here in the Northern Cape.
Script: Solar power plants are sprouting up from Upington to De Aar. This solar tower looks more like a communications mast but it’s the latest in solar technology, on its doorstep, is the Swedish test site for Solar dishes.
Link: “This is just one of 33 new renewable projects commissioned by the Department of Energy they say it is one of the best procurement policies in the world because of its transparency
Script: The Department of Energy has opened up the power game, inviting independent power producers to deliver 17800MW of renewable energy by 2030. Ian Curry says the beauty of it is that South Africa is no longer dependent on one power provider, Eskom
Ian Curry “The risk is taken by the independent power producer if I develop a project as an IPP and I mess it up I run over on time I run over on budget that impacts me and my company ..the risk is contained and it doesn’t infect the rest of the country
Script: We’re in that crisis because of Governments bad planning and a falling coal supply says Professor Wikus Van Niekerk, Head of the Solar Thermal Research group at Stellenbosch University
Wikus “Derek if you go home tonight will you have power— anybody in SA who believes we are not in an energy crisis of course is not living where we are living- …I don’t even think that Government really understands the crisis we are in
Script: Head of Living Planet Unit for the WWF, Saliem Fakir agrees
Saliem Fakir “I think we are in a crisis. If we have persistent load shedding for the next 5 years that is really putting the economy on tenter hooks. Some say we have 2% reserve margin and others say we don’t have any reserve margin so what’s being managed at the moment is really a juggling ball
Wikus “The existing power plants in Eskom will have to be winded down over the next 5- 20 years because they are very very old coal fire stations. It is actually impractical to look at a new coal fire power station or a next nuclear station because we don’t need new generation in 10 or 15 years’ time, we need it today and there are only two technologies that can provide that, its Gas and renewables .The next nuclear and coal plants are going to lag if they ever come online
Script: Both Wikus and Saliem believe that South Africa is in the perfect predicament to allow Renewable power to truly take off. It could supply 25% of our power needs. Solar Voltaic power costs have plummeted in the last 5 years making renewable energy cheaper than Coal. Graphic of Cost per Kilowatt Hour Wind 61c KWh Solar Voltaic 78c KWh Eskom 80c-R1.50KWh
Wikus “We have probably got the best solar resource in the world. So as far as renewable energy resources are concerned we are very very blessed.
Script: The beauty of Renewables is that they are spread across the country, from Wind farms in the Western Cape, to Solar Voltaic fields in the North. But they have always been unreliable because of the weather. So storage of power, is the holy grail of renewables, it’s no wonder that South African born Elon Musk’s Tesla Powerwall garnered so much attention. Concentrated Solar power with massive storage capacity, is the new kid on the block in South Africa
Wikus “Storage can last for many hours days it can even last for days- there is a plant in Spain that has the world record that can generate for 36 days continuously from only solar energy. In a thermal cycle you get 99% of that energy back, it’s a very simple very efficient energy storage system
Script: Google Map The first and largest concentrated solar plant in the Southern Hemisphere just outside Pofadder. Built by Spanish Company Abengoa for R8 Billion it came on line in April this year generating 100MW of electricity onto the national grid. That’s enough for 80,000 homes and it stores 3 hours of power. General manager Louis Van Heerden proudly says it took just 27 months to build
Louis Van Heerden “We have a conventional power station, but we are taking the burning of fossil fuels out and we are putting solar energy in to make power but also then to store energy while we are generating electricity that allows us to even when the sun goes down still provide electricity
Script: Google Map Just down the road Saudi company ACWA Power is building Bokpoort CSP, for R5 Billion, it’s the size of 100 soccer fields. CEO Nandu Bhula says it boasts the largest storage capacity
Nandu Bhula “With Bokpoort we have quite a large storage capacity 9.3 hours, and that is at 50MW full rated capacity. We have a 16 hour production capability which makes us a very reliable opportunity for the national grid so they don’t have to worry about renewable plants coming off and coming on”
Script: The most common Concentrated Solar Power is what’s known as the parabolic trough systems.
Links “The heat in here is incredible I am actually being radiated by a line of mirrors that track the sun to heat up a special fluid in these pipes to over 400 degrees as it travels to a central plant to power the turbines
Link “The heated fluid comes from the solar fields and splits, some of it is used to make steam to power the turbines over there, the rest goes to heat molten salts in those tanks which is the basis of that 9 hour storage system.
Script: The Molten salts are a mixture of common salts and once heated to 400 degrees Celsius become liquid, retaining this heat to generate steam after sunset. These tanks are filled with 38000 tons of molten salt which will last 30 years. But the outlay isn’t cheap
Louis Van Heerden “If we look at the open cycle gas turbines where Eskom burns diesel to meet the peaking period a solar thermal electric plant will produce power at a lower price compared with that option so even although you have a big capital up front you have very low running costs you have no fuel costs and it becomes quite a commercially viable option Graphic Eskom Open Gas Turbine R6KWh Concentrated Solar Power R4 KWh
Script: Once the capital costs are covered it’s hugely profitable business. It’s also the first time renewables can be counted on to supply consistent power, known as base load in energy speak.
Saliem Fakir “The fact that you can build CSP plants in 3 to 4 years it makes sense in the gap period to be able to offset the high cost of diesel. I think the beauty of CSP and why it is such an important technology is that it has base load potential just like coal plants or nuclear plants do
Link “This takes concentrated solar power to a new level, that structure is over 200 meters high no wonder it’s called tower technology “
Script: Solar towers are the new frontier of Concentrated Solar Power there only 5 others in the world. This is Khi Solar one just outside Upington also being built by Spanish Company Abengoa
Louis Van Heerden: On a parabolic trough you have a heat receiver on each mirror, here with the tower technology you have a one single receiver mounted on a tall tower ….all the mirrors or helio stats move on two axis’s reflect the energy onto that receiver and in the case of Kei one you pump water through the receiver you zap it with all of this concentrated solar it turns to steam and you run your turbine
Link: Just outside Upington these massive solar dishes also part of the race to find an efficient system to generate energy from the sun
Script: Swedish Company Riapasso have been testing the efficiency of these solar dishes for the last 4 years and will have their first installation by 2017. Ian Curry Independent power producer is one of their clients
Ian Curry ”The Sterling engine is the heart of the system and that is what converts the thermal energy of the sun to electrical energy. That large parabolic reflector that you can see there, what that does is it concentrates the solar thermal energy ….and we control that to 700 degrees Celsius that drives the Sterling engine which is a heat engine which is coupled to a generator and throughout the day the system tracks the sun
Script: The Sterling engine adapted from the original design by the Scottish engineer in the 19th centuary . It switches to gas, or even biogas, after sunset providing power 24 hours a day.
Ian Curry “The system holds the record for converting incoming solar radiation to … electricity on the grid of 33% which is remarkable compared to any other technology out there
Script: The beauty of the solar dish is that they are ideal for rural communities far from the grid. One dish generates enough to power 24 homes. You literally install as many dishes as you need. They can operate on, or off the grid
Link “These renewable energy projects are about the latest technology but they are also changing the lives of rural communities in a very meaningful way.
Script: 30% of each project is contracted to social economic development. Groblershoop the closest town to Bokpoort CSP , has 70% unemployment so when 300 people were employed to build the plant and with numerous social upliftment programs its beginning to transformed lives
Aunty “It was unbelievable for me when they came and said there is a panel for your lights and here is a TV and a radio it was unbelievable “
Louis Van Heerden “Kaxu solar one is owned by 3 entities Abengoa, the industrial development corporation and then the Kaxu community trust …the community that surrounds this project actually owns 20% of the Power plant, so over the life of the plant they will be getting dividends going to the community for projects and upliftment
Nandu Bhula “Probably what most people do not realise is that pretty much everything in the solar field has been made locally.
Script: New technology is making renewables more accessible by the year. The race is on to get off the grid, with the G8 group of nations committing to phase out fossil fuels by the end of the century.
Wikus “South Africa is ideally poised to be a major world player in this.We believe that CSP if we do it properly CSP can be the next SASOL for SA where if we make a strategic decision if we build a few gigawatt CSP power stations in SA we can establish the technology here we can become an exporter of the technology here but we need to have the big buy in.

Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 31 August 2015 Press Release: Concentrated Solar Power With even more solar radiation levels than the Sahara, South Africa has become the epicentre of a solar explosion. Renewable energy is big business and independent power producers the world over are scrambling to the Northern Cape for a spot in the sun. In a race to get off the grid, solar power stations are sprouting up from Upington to De Aar. With SA set to become a world player in the solar market, Carte Blanche asks whether load shedding could actually be a blessing in disguise? Script: Script: Nothings predictable in South Africa at the moment, except the sun is guaranteed to shine in the Northern Cape. With the second best solar radiation levels globally, even more than the Sahara, Independent power producers from around the world are scrambling to get their spot in the sun. Link “It’s the new gold rush, energy from the skies to power industry and our everyday lives. The solar explosion is happening right here in the Northern Cape. Script: Solar power plants are sprouting up from Upington to De Aar. This solar tower looks more like a communications mast but it’s the latest in solar technology, on its doorstep, is the Swedish test site for Solar dishes. Link: “This is just one of 33 new renewable projects commissioned by the Department of Energy they say it is one of the best procurement policies in the world because of its transparency Script: The Department of Energy has opened up the power game, inviting independent power producers to deliver 17800MW of renewable energy by 2030. Ian Curry says the beauty of it is that South Africa is no longer dependent on one power provider, Eskom Ian Curry “The risk is taken by the independent power producer if I develop a project as an IPP and I mess it up I run over on time I run over on budget that impacts me and my company ..the risk is contained and it doesn’t infect the rest of the country Script: We’re in that crisis because of Governments bad planning and a falling coal supply says Professor Wikus Van Niekerk, Head of the Solar Thermal Research group at Stellenbosch University Wikus “Derek if you go home tonight will you have power— anybody in SA who believes we are not in an energy crisis of course is not living where we are living- …I don’t even think that Government really understands the crisis we are in Script: Head of Living Planet Unit for the WWF, Saliem Fakir agrees Saliem Fakir “I think we are in a crisis. If we have persistent load shedding for the next 5 years that is really putting the economy on tenter hooks. Some say we have 2% reserve margin and others say we don’t have any reserve margin so what’s being managed at the moment is really a juggling ball Wikus “The existing power plants in Eskom will have to be winded down over the next 5- 20 years because they are very very old coal fire stations. It is actually impractical to look at a new coal fire power station or a next nuclear station because we don’t need new generation in 10 or 15 years’ time, we need it today and there are only two technologies that can provide that, its Gas and renewables .The next nuclear and coal plants are going to lag if they ever come online Script: Both Wikus and Saliem believe that South Africa is in the perfect predicament to allow Renewable power to truly take off. It could supply 25% of our power needs. Solar Voltaic power costs have plummeted in the last 5 years making renewable energy cheaper than Coal. Graphic of Cost per Kilowatt Hour Wind 61c KWh Solar Voltaic 78c KWh Eskom 80c-R1.50KWh Wikus “We have probably got the best solar resource in the world. So as far as renewable energy resources are concerned we are very very blessed. Script: The beauty of Renewables is that they are spread across the country, from Wind farms in the Western Cape, to Solar Voltaic fields in the North. But they have always been unreliable because of the weather. So storage of power, is the holy grail of renewables, it’s no wonder that South African born Elon Musk’s Tesla Powerwall garnered so much attention. Concentrated Solar power with massive storage capacity, is the new kid on the block in South Africa Wikus “Storage can last for many hours days it can even last for days- there is a plant in Spain that has the world record that can generate for 36 days continuously from only solar energy. In a thermal cycle you get 99% of that energy back, it’s a very simple very efficient energy storage system Script: Google Map The first and largest concentrated solar plant in the Southern Hemisphere just outside Pofadder. Built by Spanish Company Abengoa for R8 Billion it came on line in April this year generating 100MW of electricity onto the national grid. That’s enough for 80,000 homes and it stores 3 hours of power. General manager Louis Van Heerden proudly says it took just 27 months to build Louis Van Heerden “We have a conventional power station, but we are taking the burning of fossil fuels out and we are putting solar energy in to make power but also then to store energy while we are generating electricity that allows us to even when the sun goes down still provide electricity Script: Google Map Just down the road Saudi company ACWA Power is building Bokpoort CSP, for R5 Billion, it’s the size of 100 soccer fields. CEO Nandu Bhula says it boasts the largest storage capacity Nandu Bhula “With Bokpoort we have quite a large storage capacity 9.3 hours, and that is at 50MW full rated capacity. We have a 16 hour production capability which makes us a very reliable opportunity for the national grid so they don’t have to worry about renewable plants coming off and coming on” Script: The most common Concentrated Solar Power is what’s known as the parabolic trough systems. Links “The heat in here is incredible I am actually being radiated by a line of mirrors that track the sun to heat up a special fluid in these pipes to over 400 degrees as it travels to a central plant to power the turbines Link “The heated fluid comes from the solar fields and splits, some of it is used to make steam to power the turbines over there, the rest goes to heat molten salts in those tanks which is the basis of that 9 hour storage system. Script: The Molten salts are a mixture of common salts and once heated to 400 degrees Celsius become liquid, retaining this heat to generate steam after sunset. These tanks are filled with 38000 tons of molten salt which will last 30 years. But the outlay isn’t cheap Louis Van Heerden “If we look at the open cycle gas turbines where Eskom burns diesel to meet the peaking period a solar thermal electric plant will produce power at a lower price compared with that option so even although you have a big capital up front you have very low running costs you have no fuel costs and it becomes quite a commercially viable option Graphic Eskom Open Gas Turbine R6KWh Concentrated Solar Power R4 KWh Script: Once the capital costs are covered it’s hugely profitable business. It’s also the first time renewables can be counted on to supply consistent power, known as base load in energy speak. Saliem Fakir “The fact that you can build CSP plants in 3 to 4 years it makes sense in the gap period to be able to offset the high cost of diesel. I think the beauty of CSP and why it is such an important technology is that it has base load potential just like coal plants or nuclear plants do Link “This takes concentrated solar power to a new level, that structure is over 200 meters high no wonder it’s called tower technology “ Script: Solar towers are the new frontier of Concentrated Solar Power there only 5 others in the world. This is Khi Solar one just outside Upington also being built by Spanish Company Abengoa Louis Van Heerden: On a parabolic trough you have a heat receiver on each mirror, here with the tower technology you have a one single receiver mounted on a tall tower ….all the mirrors or helio stats move on two axis’s reflect the energy onto that receiver and in the case of Kei one you pump water through the receiver you zap it with all of this concentrated solar it turns to steam and you run your turbine Link: Just outside Upington these massive solar dishes also part of the race to find an efficient system to generate energy from the sun Script: Swedish Company Riapasso have been testing the efficiency of these solar dishes for the last 4 years and will have their first installation by 2017. Ian Curry Independent power producer is one of their clients Ian Curry ”The Sterling engine is the heart of the system and that is what converts the thermal energy of the sun to electrical energy. That large parabolic reflector that you can see there, what that does is it concentrates the solar thermal energy ….and we control that to 700 degrees Celsius that drives the Sterling engine which is a heat engine which is coupled to a generator and throughout the day the system tracks the sun Script: The Sterling engine adapted from the original design by the Scottish engineer in the 19th centuary . It switches to gas, or even biogas, after sunset providing power 24 hours a day. Ian Curry “The system holds the record for converting incoming solar radiation to … electricity on the grid of 33% which is remarkable compared to any other technology out there Script: The beauty of the solar dish is that they are ideal for rural communities far from the grid. One dish generates enough to power 24 homes. You literally install as many dishes as you need. They can operate on, or off the grid Link “These renewable energy projects are about the latest technology but they are also changing the lives of rural communities in a very meaningful way. Script: 30% of each project is contracted to social economic development. Groblershoop the closest town to Bokpoort CSP , has 70% unemployment so when 300 people were employed to build the plant and with numerous social upliftment programs its beginning to transformed lives Aunty “It was unbelievable for me when they came and said there is a panel for your lights and here is a TV and a radio it was unbelievable “ Louis Van Heerden “Kaxu solar one is owned by 3 entities Abengoa, the industrial development corporation and then the Kaxu community trust …the community that surrounds this project actually owns 20% of the Power plant, so over the life of the plant they will be getting dividends going to the community for projects and upliftment Nandu Bhula “Probably what most people do not realise is that pretty much everything in the solar field has been made locally. Script: New technology is making renewables more accessible by the year. The race is on to get off the grid, with the G8 group of nations committing to phase out fossil fuels by the end of the century. Wikus “South Africa is ideally poised to be a major world player in this.We believe that CSP if we do it properly CSP can be the next SASOL for SA where if we make a strategic decision if we build a few gigawatt CSP power stations in SA we can establish the technology here we can become an exporter of the technology here but we need to have the big buy in. metadata.Summary: South Africa has 33 Renewable Energy power plants commissioned and by the end of next year there will be enough plants online to generate the same amount of power as Koeberg. By 2030 they will generate 17 800 MW of power. Globally there is a move towards renewable energy, the G7 announced this week that they intend to stop using all fossil fuels by the end of the century. South Africa is in a very unique position in that most of the country has sufficient sunshine all year to be totally solar powered. We can solve our electricity needs with Renewables which raises the question why we are pursuing Nuclear power at the cost of 1 Trillion Rand and that's without the costs of disposaling of the nuclear rods. Fracking for natural gas also makes no economic sense when the world price of oil is dropping.Since 2010 we have been embracing Renewables, this week Minister of Energy Tina Joemat-Petterssen commissioned 13 new renewable projects. Concentrated Solar Power or CSP has changed the whole solar power industry because its made solar energy storable and stable.
metadata.Further information: Concentrated Solar Power or CSP is the new kid on the block when it comes to renewable energy. It focuses the solar energy and is able to store it for several hours after sunset and because of how it is stored it is more stable and accessible that coal fired power stations. A CSP plant can be switched onto the grid within 15 minutes whereas a coal plant takes hours to fire up. There are 7 CSP projects being built in South Africa, KaXu Solar 1 came online in March this year and producers 100 MWs and has 5 hours of power generation after dark. Bokspoort is nearing completion and will have 9 hours of storage generating 50MW power. Bokspoort has the largest storage capacity in the world. Currently Eskom is burning the reserve generators to keep the lights on but these are fired by diesel and gas and costing a whopping R5 KW hour.CSP wind and Solar Voltaic electricity can supply that additional power at one fifth of the cost. Wind power costs 68c a KW hour and Solar Voltaic 85c a KW hour. Globally 90% of the coal reserves will be economically exhausted by 2048 meaning that it will be so expensive to extract it won’t be economically viable. In South Africa we are on a plateau of Coal production but from here on it will start declining. Medupi will run out of coal half way through it life span. Currently it is estimated electricity generated by coal costs R1.05 but this cost will continue to rise. Photovoltic and wind energy is already cheaper that Coal, and CSP solar power will get cheaper as technology advances. Swedish Company Ripasso which has used technology originally designed for the military and developed it for solar power generation which outstrips the performance of current solar voltaic panels. It consists of 100 sq meter solar dishes which rotate following the path of the sun, capturing 35% of solar energy which is then drives a Stirling engine. Stirling engines have no carbon emissions. The project has been piloted for the last 4 years in the Kalahari. The amount of power generated is 35% , 10 % higher than Solarvoltaic panels which capture only 23% and convert to the grid on 15%. Each dish can generate 75-85 megawatts of power which is enough for 24 average households for 1 year. If the same amount of power was generated by coal power station it would emit 81 metric tonnes of CO2 Carbon Emissions. They have a hybridized system that switches over to fuel to keep running at night. This system gives you power for 24 hours. Any kind of fuel can be used, from biofuel to gas. KaXu Solar One plant it is a 100MW concentrated solar power (CSP) on a 1,100ha site. It's the first CSP plant in South Africa to using parabolic trough technology. It supplies clean energy to approximately 90,000 African homes while offsetting 315,000t of CO2 emissions per year. Khi Solar 1 also in partership with Spanish Company Abengoa uses tower technology and is about to come online. The 4th project is purely South African and based at Stellenbosch University called Helio100. It is using entirely SA labour and materials and developing CSP Tower technology with much smaller dishes close to the ground which can project from 1km from any solar tower. It is part of the Solar Thermal Energy Research Group, the largest research unit of its kind worldwide.
